title: The U That Guards G
kidRule: G likes to go soft before E and I. So a quiet U stands in between to keep the G hard, as in GUITAR and GUESS! At the end of a word, the team G-U-E says a hard G too, as in LEAGUE.
hint: We hear a hard '/g/' here, but a quiet helper letter stands right after the G. Which letter is it?
reminder: A quiet U stands right after the G to keep it hard: G-U.

check.question: Why does GUITAR have a quiet U after the G?
check.correctAnswer: The U keeps the G hard, so it does not go soft before the I!
distractors: Because the U makes the I say its name
Because every word that starts with G needs a U

words.def: A musical instrument with strings that you play with your fingers.
words.sent: My uncle plays the guitar around the campfire.
words.story: Most of these instruments have six strings. The name came to English from the Spanish word 'guitarra'!
words.card: The rock s*tar* strummed a *guitar* made of spaghetti!

words.def: To give an answer when you are not sure that it is right.
words.sent: Can you guess how many beans are in the jar?
words.story: Scientists have a special name for a careful guess: a hypothesis. Then they test it to see if it is right!
words.card: *Guess* who made this m*ess*? The dog in the pirate hat!

words.def: Having done something wrong, or feeling bad because you did.
words.sent: The puppy looked guilty beside the chewed slipper.
words.story: When a dog looks guilty, it is mostly reacting to its owner's voice and face. Dogs give that same look even when they have done nothing wrong!
words.card: The *guilty* kitten hid under the qu*ilt* with jam on her whiskers!

words.def: The soft part inside your mouth that you use to taste, lick, and talk.
words.sent: The puppy licked my hand with its warm tongue.
words.story: A giraffe's tongue is about as long as your arm, and it is a dark bluish-purple color!
words.card: My *tongue* felt like it weighed a *ton* after forty ice creams!

words.def: Clothes or other things you wear so that nobody knows who you are.
words.sent: The detective wore a silly mustache as a disguise.
words.story: Some animals wear a disguise! The decorator crab sticks bits of seaweed and sponge onto its shell so it is hard to spot.
words.card: My *disguise* was a *dis*h of spaghetti on my head!

words.def: A group of teams that play games against each other.
words.sent: Our soccer team is in first place in the league.
words.story: Long ago this word was also a measure of distance, about three miles. That is the meaning in the famous book 'Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea'!
words.card: The ladybug *league* plays soccer on a *lea*f!

words.def: Help and advice that shows you what to do or which way to go.
words.sent: With my teacher's guidance, I built a model bridge.
words.story: Baby sea turtles need no guidance to find the ocean. They hatch at night and crawl toward the brightest part of the sky, which is over the water!
words.card: With a little *guidance*, the hippo learned to *dance* on a drum!

words.sent: He gave a vague answer and pointed somewhere over the hill.
words.story: This word comes from the Latin 'vagus', which means wandering. A vague answer wanders around and never gets to the point!
words.card: The map was so *vague* that we found a *va*nilla swamp instead of the treasure!

words.def: A feeling of being very, very tired.
words.sent: After the long hike, fatigue made my legs feel like noodles.
words.story: Yawning is a sign of fatigue, and it is catching! Seeing someone yawn can make you yawn too, and dogs can even catch yawns from people.
words.card: *Fatigue* made the *tig*er fall asleep in his soup!

words.def: To make someone very curious and interested.
words.sent: Secret tunnels intrigue my sister more than anything.
words.story: This word comes from the Latin 'intricare', which means to tangle. A puzzle that tangles up your thinking is sure to intrigue you!
